item.title: Swift Selectors: Bridging Objective-C APIs for Modern Development
item.description:
“Swift Selectors: Bridging Objective-C APIs for Modern Development”

While Swift itself does not directly utilize selectors, many Objective-C based APIs, particularly those involving timers and the target-action pattern, rely on them. Swift provides the Selector type to interface with these APIs seamlessly. This post delves into how to effectively use selectors in Swift, covering syntax changes across versions, common pitfalls, and best practices for interacting with Objective-C frameworks.

The Role of Selectors in Swift

Selectors in Swift act as a bridge to Objective-C’s runtime. They represent a method’s name, allowing dynamic invocation. When working with APIs like Timer, UIBarButtonItem, or gesture recognizers, you’ll often need to specify a target method using a selector.

item.title: Unrecognized Selector Sent to Instance Error in Swift Objective-C Explained
item.description:
“Unrecognized Selector Sent to Instance Error in Swift Objective-C Explained”

Encountering an “unrecognized selector sent to instance” error in your Swift or Objective-C project can halt development progress. This common runtime issue signifies that an object received a message (method call) it doesn’t know how to handle. Let’s delve into the various causes and effective strategies for diagnosing and resolving this problem.

The core of this error message, such as [UITableViewCellContentView image]: unrecognized selector sent to instance, pinpoints the object (UITableViewCellContentView) and the specific method (image) that was called but not implemented by that object. Understanding the context of this message is the crucial first step towards a solution.
